- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) and forecast is below recent high, adjust upward by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) and forecast is above recent low, adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid overcorrection.
- Avoid forecasting sharp spikes: if last 3–5 prices show rapid upward movement, cap forecast rise at 10% above prior peak to prevent overshoot.
- If sentiment is volatile (alternating 0.2–0.8) and forecast is trending, apply mean reversion: if forecast is 3σ above mean, reduce by 1–3 points; if 3σ below, increase by 1–3 points.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 1–2% to avoid lagged overreaction.
- If sentiment history shows recent reversal (e.g., 0.9 → 0.1), reduce forecast slope to avoid “sentiment lag” bias.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is high, apply downward bias correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% from forecast to reflect subdued market sentiment.
